title: Retries and idempotency at a pipeline boundary
summary: Hybrid / System Design / Pipeline reliability / Failure and replay

children.text: A job writes output successfully but crashes before acknowledging completion. The scheduler retries it. How do you avoid duplicate data?

items: Identify the crash boundary between write and acknowledgement.
Reuse an immutable batch identity across retries.
Define how the sink detects or overwrites an already committed batch.
Retry transient faults with limits; surface invalid data separately.

children.text: Retrying safely requires a stable identity for the logical work and an atomic or deduplicated write contract. A new random run ID for each retry does not identify the same logical batch. The configuration below is a design example, not an executable product-specific API.

Watch for this
children.text: A processed-batch check followed by an unrelated write is vulnerable to races. The commit/marker must share the required transaction boundary or use another proven atomic protocol.

items: What happens when two workers retry the same batch at the same time?
Reason about failure boundaries and replay.
Distinguish a retry policy from idempotent effects.
